$comment: Consumers of the canonical Snyk policy in snyk-policy/base.snyk.
Steady state: a repo's .snyk is [canonical block][# repo-specific][tail].
The sync regenerates the block and preserves the tail byte-for-byte, so a
repo only appears here to (a) opt in, (b) carry a note rendered into the
block, or (c) declare a ONE-TIME migration for a file that predates the
convention.
A migrate directive DISARMS ITSELF: it fires only while fromSha still
matches the file on main. Once the first fan-out has merged the blob
changes, so a forgotten entry here cannot delete policy the repo added
later. The check reports spent directives so they can be tidied up.
migrate.fromSha — the git blob SHA of the .snyk this directive was written
against. The migration runs ONLY on an exact match, which makes it
exactly-once: after the first fan-out merges, the blob changes and the
directive can never fire again. Do not derive converted-state from the
file's contents instead — a consumer that edits the canonical block would
make a spent directive look live and a "none" tail would delete policy
added since. Refresh fromSha (gh api /repos/digitalnsw/<repo>/contents/
.snyk --jq .sha) if the file changes on main before the migration lands.
migrate.tail — how to derive the tail the first time a repo is converted:
"none"            the whole existing file is canonical-shaped; drop it
{ "from": "..." } tail starts at the first line containing this string
Once the migration has merged the directive is inert and can be deleted.
A stale directive (fromSha no longer matches, file not in canonical shape)
is REFUSED and reported — never guessed at.
migrate: "manual" excludes a repo from automated conversion entirely. It
is still checked, and reported, but never rewritten.
Adding a repo: add a key here. The sync creates .snyk if it is absent —
unless it already has a .snyk predating this convention, in which case give
it a migrate directive (with fromSha) for its first fan-out only.
The first 13 consumers were converted on 2026-09-04, so no directive
remains from that round. The 12 automated ones migrated through the
fan-out; dtl-sandbox was converted by hand (digitalnsw/dtl-sandbox#54)
because its path-scoping rationale sat above `ignore:`, where the
canonical block now lives.
2026-09-07: ten more repos were enrolled, all of which had NO .snyk at
all, so the sync creates each file and none needed a migrate directive.
nswds-devops is now a consumer of the policy it publishes: the fan-out
treats it like any other repo, and a .snyk change here does not match
the workflow's `snyk-policy/**` path filter, so it cannot re-trigger
itself.
2026-09-07 (second round): the last six repos were enrolled, so the
whole 29-repo fleet is now covered. They are plain keys, NOT migrate
directives, and that is deliberate: each already ends with the
'  # repo-specific' marker and carries nothing after it, so splitAtMarker
succeeds and selectTail returns 'steady' with an empty tail. Verified by
calling selectTail and compose directly: a bare key and a migrate
directive with tail 'none' render byte-identical files.
A directive here would have been strictly worse. It buys nothing, and it
adds a failure mode a plain key does not have: these files predate the
'generated from nswds-devops' sentinel, so isConverted() is false, and if
one of their blobs moved before the fan-out evaluated it, selectTail would
REFUSE that repo rather than sync it. Reserve migrate directives for files
that genuinely lack the marker.
Their two nanoid ignores are dropped with the rest of the pre-canonical
block, and that loses nothing: all six resolve nanoid 3.3.18, which
carries both fixes -- -894 was backported in 3.3.16, and -897's
customRandom size guard landed in 3.3.17. Scanning all six with
--ignore-policy confirms neither advisory still fires.
